content.text:
IndexedDB snapshots now keep `Map` and `Set` values through save and restore. I couldn't build or run anything, so this is untested.

**Cause:** the shared serializer in `packages/isomorphic/utilityScriptSerializers.ts` had no `Map` or `Set` case. Both fell through to the generic object case, which only walks own enumerable properties, so they came out as `{}`.

**Changes:**
- **Serializer:** `serializeAsCallArgument` takes a new opt-in option, `mapsAndSets`. When it's on, a `Map` encodes as `{ m: [{k, v}...], id }` and a `Set` as `{ se: [...], id }`. The encoding goes through the same visited-ID tracking as arrays and objects, so cycles and shared references still work.
- **Parser:** `parseEvaluationResultValue` rebuilds a real `Map` or `Set` from those two encodings. Nothing else produces them, so the parser change has no effect on existing data.
- **IndexedDB snapshot:** `_trySerialize` in `packages/injected/src/storageScript.ts` passes `{ mapsAndSets: true }`. A `Map` or `Set` isn't a plain object, so it takes the encoded path and is stored in `valueEncoded` or `keyEncoded`.

Page evaluation doesn't pass the option, so a `Map` or `Set` returned from `evaluate` still becomes `{}`, as the issue requires. The `valueEncoded` and `keyEncoded` fields are typed `any` in the protocol validator, so the protocol needs no changes.

I didn't add a test.
